summary: Requalify unknown-duration MP4 chapter clocks against positive composition endpoints
before: Runtime baseline: 1 playback control passes and chapter-clock test fails. Twelve unknown/zero movie-duration cases confuse +200ms composition offset with a 60ms decode-duration bound; both parser wrappers report 200ms chapters as 20us (movie-clock case) or 2000s (10MHz case). Six known-movie controls and all 18 actual software playback controls pass.
after: 45 distinct checks pass across 8 targets, including 2 new tests. Eighteen synthetic movies preserve 200/220/240ms chapter names/moments in both supported clocks and both parser wrappers, exact software YUV/RGB, 260ms native duration, 180 seek positions, rewind and EOF. Related unknown chapter clocks, hidden-frame endpoint bounds, finite/open edits, empty fragments and baseline MP4 checks pass. Locked offline no-default-features core build check passes.
tests_run: cargo test --locked --offline --no-default-features --features player --no-fail-fast --test mp4_chapter_composition --test mp4_unknown_movie_chapters --test mp4 --test mp4_nondisplay_endpoint --test mp4_presentation_endpoint --test mp4_open_ended_edit --test mp4_empty_fragment --test mp4_edit_window_eof
limitations: The clock-selection heuristic remains compatibility behavior for two authored chpl conventions; ambiguous small timestamps cannot always distinguish clocks.
With all presentation headers unstated, the endpoint is a nominal index estimate and cannot prove display output from decode-only packets.
No new visual UI, performance, full-project green or GPU parity claim. Historical unrelated baseline failures remain separate.
uncounted: Positive-CTS qualification and repair of FVID-0401 clock bound
